1→// This is your Prisma schema file,
     2→// learn more about it in the docs: https://pris.ly/d/prisma-schema
     3→
     4→generator client {
     5→  provider = "prisma-client-js"
     6→}
     7→
     8→datasource db {
     9→  provider  = "postgresql"
    10→  url       = env("DATABASE_URL")
    11→  directUrl = env("DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED") // Direct connection for migrations (bypasses pooler)
    12→}
    13→
    14→/// Package table - stores NPM package metadata (package-level)
    15→model Package {
    16→  id String @id @default(cuid())
    17→
    18→  // NPM Metadata
    19→  npmPackageName String   @unique @map("npm_package_name") @db.VarChar(214)
    20→  npmVersion     String   @map("npm_version") @db.VarChar(50)
    21→  npmPublishedAt DateTime @map("npm_published_at")
    22→  npmDescription String?  @map("npm_description") @db.Text
    23→  npmRepository  Json?    @map("npm_repository") @db.JsonB
    24→  npmHomepage    String?  @map("npm_homepage") @db.Text
    25→  npmLicense     String?  @map("npm_license") @db.VarChar(50)
    26→  npmKeywords    String[] @default([]) @map("npm_keywords") @db.Text
    27→  npmReadme      String?  @map("npm_readme") @db.Text
    28→  npmAuthor      Json?    @map("npm_author") @db.JsonB
    29→  npmMaintainers Json?    @map("npm_maintainers") @db.JsonB
    30→
    31→  // TPMJS Package-Level Metadata
    32→  category       String   @db.VarChar(50)
    33→  env            Json?    @db.JsonB // Environment variables (shared across tools)
    34→  frameworks     String[] @default([]) @db.Text
    35→  tier           String   @db.VarChar(20) // 'minimal' | 'rich'
    36→  discoveryMethod String  @map("discovery_method") @db.VarChar(20) // 'keyword' | 'changes-feed'
    37→  isOfficial     Boolean  @default(false) @map("is_official")
    38→
    39→  // Package Metrics
    40→  npmDownloadsLastMonth Int? @default(0) @map("npm_downloads_last_month")
    41→  githubStars           Int? @default(0) @map("github_stars")
    42→
    43→  // Timestamps
    44→  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
    45→  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
    46→
    47→  // Relations
    48→  tools Tool[]
    49→
    50→  @@index([category])
    51→  @@index([isOfficial])
    52→  @@index([npmDownloadsLastMonth])
    53→  @@index([createdAt])
    54→  @@map("packages")
    55→}
    56→
    57→/// Tool table - stores individual tools within packages
    58→model Tool {
    59→  id String @id @default(cuid())
    60→
    61→  // Package Relation
    62→  packageId String  @map("package_id")
    63→  package   Package @relation(fields: [packageId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
    64→
    65→  // Tool Identity
    66→  name String @db.VarChar(100) // e.g., "helloWorldTool", "default"
    67→
    68→  // Tool Metadata
    69→  description String @db.Text
    70→  parameters  Json?  @db.JsonB // Legacy/fallback - author-provided parameters array
    71→  returns     Json?  @db.JsonB // @deprecated - will be auto-extracted in future
    72→  aiAgent     Json?  @map("ai_agent") @db.JsonB // @deprecated - will be auto-extracted in future
    73→
    74→  // Schema Extraction Fields
    75→  inputSchema                Json?     @map("input_schema") @db.JsonB // Full JSON Schema from executor
    76→  schemaSource               String?   @map("schema_source") @db.VarChar(20) // 'extracted' | 'author' | null
    77→  schemaExtractedAt          DateTime? @map("schema_extracted_at") // Only updated on successful extraction
    78→  schemaExtractionAttemptAt  DateTime? @map("schema_extraction_attempt_at") // Updated on every attempt (for rate limiting)
    79→  schemaExtractionError      String?   @map("schema_extraction_error") @db.Text // Error message from last failed attempt
    80→
    81→  // Tool Discovery Fields
    82→  toolDiscoverySource String? @map("tool_discovery_source") @db.VarChar(20) // 'auto' | 'manual' | null
    83→
    84→  // Tool Metrics
    85→  qualityScore Decimal? @map("quality_score") @db.Decimal(3, 2) // 0.00 to 1.00
    86→  likeCount    Int      @default(0) @map("like_count")
    87→
    88→  // Health Status Fields
    89→  importHealth     HealthStatus? @default(UNKNOWN) @map("import_health")
    90→  executionHealth  HealthStatus? @default(UNKNOWN) @map("execution_health")
    91→  lastHealthCheck  DateTime?     @map("last_health_check")
    92→  healthCheckError String?       @map("health_check_error") @db.Text
    93→
    94→  // Timestamps
    95→  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
    96→  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
    97→
    98→  // View tracking (denormalized, rolled up daily)
    99→  viewCount      Int      @default(0) @map("view_count")
   100→
   101→  // Execution tracking (denormalized, rolled up daily)
   102→  executionCount Int      @default(0) @map("execution_count")
   103→
   104→  // Rating aggregates
   105→  averageRating Decimal? @map("average_rating") @db.Decimal(2, 1) // 1.0 to 5.0
   106→  ratingCount   Int      @default(0) @map("rating_count")
   107→  reviewCount   Int      @default(0) @map("review_count")
   108→
   109→  // Relations
   110→  simulations     Simulation[]
   111→  healthChecks    HealthCheck[]
   112→  collections     CollectionTool[]
   113→  agents          AgentTool[]
   114→  likes           ToolLike[]
   115→  ratings         ToolRating[]
   116→  reviews         ToolReview[]
   117→  skillsCache     ToolSkillsCache?
   118→  skillQuestions  SkillQuestionTool[]
   119→
   120→  @@unique([packageId, name])
   121→  @@index([qualityScore])
   122→  @@index([likeCount])
   123→  @@index([averageRating])
   124→  @@index([ratingCount])
   125→  @@index([viewCount])
   126→  @@index([executionCount])
   127→  @@index([reviewCount])
   128→  @@index([importHealth])
   129→  @@index([executionHealth])
   130→  @@index([lastHealthCheck])
   131→  @@map("tools")
   132→}
   133→
   134→/// Sync checkpoints - tracks progress of sync workers
   135→model SyncCheckpoint {
   136→  id String @id @default(cuid())
   137→
   138→  source     String   @unique @db.VarChar(50) // 'changes-feed' | 'keyword-search' | 'metrics'
   139→  checkpoint Json     @db.JsonB // Stores last sequence, timestamp, etc.
   140→  updatedAt  DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
   141→
   142→  @@map("sync_checkpoints")
   143→}
   144→
   145→/// Sync logs - audit trail of sync operations
   146→model SyncLog {
   147→  id String @id @default(cuid())
   148→
   149→  source    String   @db.VarChar(50) // 'changes-feed' | 'keyword-search' | 'metrics'
   150→  status    String   @db.VarChar(20) // 'success' | 'error' | 'partial'
   151→  processed Int      @default(0) // Number of packages processed
   152→  skipped   Int      @default(0) // Number of packages skipped
   153→  errors    Int      @default(0) // Number of errors encountered
   154→  message   String?  @db.Text // Error message or summary
   155→  metadata  Json?    @db.JsonB // Additional context
   156→  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
   157→
   158→  @@index([source])
   159→  @@index([status])
   160→  @@index([createdAt])
   161→  @@map("sync_logs")
   162→}
   163→
   164→/// Simulations - tracks tool playground executions
   165→model Simulation {
   166→  id String @id @default(cuid())
   167→
   168→  // Relations
   169→  toolId String @map("tool_id")
   170→  tool   Tool   @relation(fields: [toolId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
   171→
   172→  // Request data
   173→  userPrompt String  @map("user_prompt") @db.Text
   174→  parameters Json?   @db.JsonB
   175→  ipAddress  String? @map("ip_address") @db.VarChar(45)
   176→  userAgent  String? @map("user_agent") @db.Text
   177→
   178→  // Results
   179→  status          String  @db.VarChar(20) // pending|running|success|error|timeout
   180→  executionTimeMs Int?    @map("execution_time_ms")
   181→  output          Json?   @db.JsonB
   182→  error           String? @db.Text
   183→
   184→  // AI metadata
   185→  agentSteps Int     @default(0) @map("agent_steps")
   186→  model      String? @db.VarChar(50)
   187→
   188→  // Relations
   189→  tokenUsage   TokenUsage?
   190→  logs         ExecutionLog[]
   191→
   192→  createdAt   DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at")
   193→  completedAt DateTime? @map("completed_at")
   194→
   195→  @@index([toolId])
   196→  @@index([status])
   197→  @@index([ipAddress, createdAt]) // For rate limiting
   198→  @@map("simulations")
   199→}
   200→
   201→/// Token usage - tracks token consumption per simulation
   202→model TokenUsage {
   203→  id String @id @default(cuid())
   204→
   205→  simulationId String     @unique @map("simulation_id")
   206→  simulation   Simulation @relation(fields: [simulationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
   207→
   208→  inputTokens    Int      @default(0) @map("input_tokens")
   209→  toolDescTokens Int      @default(0) @map("tool_desc_tokens")
   210→  schemaTokens   Int      @default(0) @map("schema_tokens")
   211→  outputTokens   Int      @default(0) @map("output_tokens")
   212→  totalTokens    Int      @default(0) @map("total_tokens")
   213→  estimatedCost  Decimal? @map("estimated_cost") @db.Decimal(10, 6)
   214→
   215→  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
   216→  @@map("token_usage")
   217→}
   218→
   219→/// Execution logs - detailed logs for each simulation
   220→model ExecutionLog {
   221→  id String @id @default(cuid())
   222→
   223→  simulationId String     @map("simulation_id")
   224→  simulation   Simulation @relation(fields: [simulationId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
   225→
   226→  timestamp DateTime @default(now())
   227→  level     String   @db.VarChar(20) // info|warning|error|debug
   228→  event     String   @db.VarChar(50)
   229→  message   String   @db.Text
   230→  metadata  Json?    @db.JsonB
   231→
   232→  @@index([simulationId])
   233→  @@map("execution_logs")
   234→}
   235→
   236→/// HealthCheck table - tracks full audit history of health checks
   237→model HealthCheck {
   238→  id String @id @default(cuid())
   239→
   240→  // Relations
   241→  toolId String @map("tool_id")
   242→  tool   Tool   @relation(fields: [toolId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
   243→
   244→  // Check metadata
   245→  checkType     HealthCheckType @map("check_type")
   246→  triggerSource String          @map("trigger_source") @db.VarChar(50) // 'sync' | 'manual' | 'daily-cron'
   247→
   248→  // Import check results
   249→  importStatus HealthStatus @map("import_status")
   250→  importError  String?      @map("import_error") @db.Text
   251→  importTimeMs Int?         @map("import_time_ms")
   252→
   253→  // Execution check results
   254→  executionStatus HealthStatus @map("execution_status")
   255→  executionError  String?      @map("execution_error") @db.Text
   256→  executionTimeMs Int?         @map("execution_time_ms")
   257→  testParameters  Json?        @map("test_parameters") @db.JsonB
   258→
   259→  // Overall status
   260→  overallStatus HealthStatus @map("overall_status")
   261→
   262→  // Timestamps
   263→  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
   264→
   265→  @@index([toolId])
   266→  @@index([checkType])
   267→  @@index([overallStatus])
   268→  @@index([createdAt])
   269→  @@map("health_checks")
   270→}
   271→
   272→/// Health status enum - tracks health check results
   273→enum HealthStatus {
   274→  UNKNOWN // Not yet checked
   275→  HEALTHY // Passed health check
   276→  BROKEN  // Failed health check
   277→}
   278→
   279→/// Health check type enum - types of health checks performed

572→ The Agent Sandbox is a Deno-based execution server that gives each agent 573→ conversation its own{' '} 574→ persistent workspace directory. Unlike 575→ the default stateless executor where each tool call is independent, the sandbox 576→ preserves files across tool calls so agents can perform multi-step workflows. 577→

579→ A file written in the first turn of a conversation is still there in the tenth turn. 580→ A git repo cloned in one step can be modified and committed in the next. This is 581→ what makes agentic coding workflows possible. 582→

The full git workflow within a 596→ conversation. 597→ 598→ 599→ Tools that read and write files need shared state. ## Comprehensive Analysis: Executors and Sandbox in TPMJS

Based on my thorough exploration of the codebase, here's a complete picture of how executors and sandbox work in the system:

---

### 1. **Prisma Schema Fields (Database Level)**

The agent model in `/packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma` (lines 608-677) includes:

```prisma
executorType         String?    @map("executor_type") @db.VarChar(50)
executorConfig       Json?      @map("executor_config") @db.JsonB
envVars              Json?      @map("env_vars") @db.JsonB
```

The **Collection** model (lines 484-558) has identical fields. This enables a **cascade hierarchy**: Agent → Collection → System Default.

---

### 2. **Type Definitions** (`packages/types/src/executor.ts`)

There are **three executor types**:

| Type | Use Case | Config Fields |
|------|----------|---------------|
| `default` | Stateless (Railway executor via package-executor) | None |
| `custom_url` | Custom HTTP executor endpoint | `url` (required), `apiKey` (optional) |
| `sandbox` | Stateful sessions with persistent filesystem | `url` (optional, falls back to `AGENT_SANDBOX_URL`), `apiKey` (optional) |

Key schemas:
- **ExecutorTypeSchema**: `z.enum(['default', 'custom_url', 'sandbox'])`
- **SandboxExecutorConfig**: Requires `sessionId` in execute requests (in addition to base `ExecuteToolRequest`)
- **ExecutorConfig**: Discriminated union that validates the shape based on type

---

### 3. **Executor Resolution Logic** (`apps/web/src/lib/executors/index.ts`)

**Core Functions:**

- **`parseExecutorConfig(executorType, executorConfig)`** (lines 83-119)
  - Safely parses database JSON to strongly-typed config
  - Returns `null` for invalid configs, default for 'default' type

- **`resolveExecutorConfig(agentConfig, collectionConfig)`** (lines 61-77)
  - **Cascade priority**: Agent (highest) → Collection (medium) → System default (lowest)
  - Non-null, non-'default' configs take precedence
  - Used during tool building to determine which executor each tool gets

- **`executeWithExecutor(config, request, sessionId?)`** (lines 432-470)
  - Routes to appropriate executor based on config type:
    - `sandbox` → calls `executeWithSandbox()` (requires `sessionId`)
    - `custom_url` → calls `executeWithCustomUrl()` 
    - `default` → calls `executePackage()` (stateless Railway executor)

**Sandbox-Specific Functions:**

- **`resolveSandboxUrl(config)`** (lines 200-202): Returns `config.url || process.env.AGENT_SANDBOX_URL || null`
- **`createSandboxSession(url, apiKey, sessionId, timeoutSeconds?)`** (lines 208-269): Idempotent session creation with retry logic
- **`executeWithSandbox(url, apiKey, request, sessionId, timeout?)`** (lines 313-422): Includes retry on 429/502/503 and network errors

---

### 4. **Tool Building** (`apps/web/src/lib/agents/build-tools.ts`)

**Key Function: `buildAgentTools(agent, callerEnvVars?, sessionId?)`** (lines 246-311)

**How it works:**

1. **Parses agent-level executor config** → applies to ALL tools
2. **For each collection in agent:**
   - Parses collection-level executor config
   - **Resolves config** (agent > collection > default)
   - Parses and **merges env vars** (collection base + agent overrides)
   - Builds tool definitions with resolved executor + merged env vars + sessionId
3. **For individual agent tools:**
   - Uses agent config or default (no collection context)
   - Uses only agent env vars (no collection merging)

**Sandbox Integration:**
- `sessionId` is passed through to `createToolDefinition()` 
- `createToolDefinition()` passes `sessionId` to `executeWithExecutor()` for sandbox requests

**Environment Variable Cascade:**
```javascript
// Collection env vars (base)
{ "API_KEY": "coll-key", "REGION": "us-east-1" }

// Agent env vars (overrides)
{ "API_KEY": "agent-key", "DEBUG": "true" }

// Result: Agent overrides collection for same keys, unique keys merged
{ "API_KEY": "agent-key", "REGION": "us-east-1", "DEBUG": "true" }
```

---

### 5. **Agent Creation/Editing** 

**At Creation Time** (`/api/agents` POST route):
- **NOTE:** `executorType` and `executorConfig` are **NOT** in `CreateAgentSchema` (lines 32-50 of `packages/types/src/agent.ts`)
- Agents are created with model config only, executor config comes later via updates

**At Update Time** (`UpdateAgentSchema`):
```typescript
executorType: ExecutorTypeSchema.nullable().optional(),
executorConfig: ExecutorConfigUpdateSchema,  // { url?, apiKey? }
envVars: z.record(z.string(), z.string()).nullable().optional(),
```

**In UI** (`/dashboard/agents/new/page.tsx`):
- New agent form only shows: name, uid, description, provider, model, systemPrompt, temperature, max tool calls, context messages
- **No executor configuration shown** at creation
- Users configure executor after creation (on agent details page - not provided in your search results, but likely exists)

---

### 6. **Conversation Execution Flow** (`/api/agents/[id]/conversation/[conversationId]` POST)

**Sandbox Setup** (lines 366-397):

```typescript
let sessionId: string | undefined;
if (agent.executorType === 'sandbox') {
  const sandboxConfig = parseExecutorConfig(agent.executorType, agent.executorConfig);
  if (sandboxConfig && sandboxConfig.type === 'sandbox') {
    const sandboxUrl = resolveSandboxUrl(sandboxConfig);
    if (!sandboxUrl) {
      // Error: AGENT_SANDBOX_URL not configured
    }
    sessionId = `${agent.id}:${conversationId}`;
    // Create/resume session before tool building
    await createSandboxSession(sandboxUrl, sandboxConfig.apiKey, sessionId);
  }
}

// Build tools with sessionId
const tools = buildAgentTools(agent, callerEnvVars, sessionId);
```

**Key Details:**
- Sandbox session is created/resumed **before** streaming begins
- sessionId format: `{agentId}:{conversationId}` (stable across multiple messages)
- Session creation is idempotent (extending TTL on subsequent calls)
- Every tool call includes `sessionId` in the executor request

---

### 7. **URL References in Codebase**

**Environment Variables:**
- **`AGENT_SANDBOX_URL`** (web app): Falls back URL when agent doesn't specify custom sandbox
  - Used in `resolveSandboxUrl()` at runtime
  - Documented in `/docs/executors/sandbox/page.tsx` (line 977)
  
- **`SANDBOX_EXECUTOR_URL`** (via `package-executor`): 
  - Not directly referenced in web app (abstracted in `@tpmjs/package-executor`)
  - This is the Railway executor endpoint used by default executor

**Configuration URLs:**
- Agent/Collection can specify custom URLs in `executorConfig.url`
- Sandbox: Optional (falls back to `AGENT_SANDBOX_URL` env var)
- Custom URL: Required

---

### 8. **Sandbox Documentation** (`/docs/executors/sandbox/page.tsx`)

Comprehensive guide showing:
- **Config cascade** (lines 245-255): Agent overrides Collection overrides Default
- **Session lifecycle**: Sessions persist for 1 hour by default, destroyed on conversation delete
- **Session endpoints**: POST/GET/DELETE `/sessions/{sessionId}`
- **Execute Tool API**: POST `/execute-tool` with `sessionId` parameter
- **Limits**: 100MB disk per session, 50 concurrent sessions, 1hr TTL
- **Environment variables**: `EXECUTOR_API_KEY`, `MAX_CONCURRENT_SESSIONS`, `DEFAULT_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, etc.

---

### 9. **Workflow Diagram (from docs)**

```
User Message
    ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  TPMJS Web App (Next.js)            │
│  1. Create/resume sandbox session   │
│  2. Stream AI response              │
│  3. Route tool calls to sandbox     │
└──────────────┬──────────────────────┘
               │ POST /execute-tool
               │ { sessionId, params }
               ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Agent Sandbox Server (Deno)        │
│  Session: agent123:conv456          │
│  /workspace/ (persistent)           │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 10. **Key Architectural Insights**

1. **No executor config at agent creation** — only settable on updates
2. **Cascade resolution is per-tool** — different tools in same agent can come from different collections with different executors
3. **Session ID stability** — `agentId:conversationId` ensures same workspace across multiple message turns
4. **Idempotent session creation** — calling create again just extends TTL
5. **Environment variable isolation** — set per-execution, cleaned up afterward
6. **Fallback chain** — Agent config → Collection config → `AGENT_SANDBOX_URL` → error
7. **Retry resilience** — Sandbox executor retries on 429 (capacity), 502/503 (transient), and network errors

---

### Summary Table

| Concept | Where Stored | Where Used | Cascade? |
|---------|--------------|-----------|----------|
| `executorType` | Agent/Collection DB | Tool building, routing | Yes (Agent → Collection → Default) |
| `executorConfig` | Agent/Collection DB (JSON) | URL resolution, auth | Yes |
| `envVars` | Agent/Collection DB (JSON) | Tool execution | Yes (Agent overrides Collection) |
| `sessionId` | Not stored (computed) | Sandbox requests | Per conversation |
| `AGENT_SANDBOX_URL` | Env var | Fallback for sandbox URL | No (static) |
| `SANDBOX_EXECUTOR_URL` | Env var (in package-executor) | Default executor routing | No (static) |

This architecture enables flexible, hot-swappable executors while maintaining backward compatibility with the default stateless executor.

## Comprehensive Analysis: Executors and Sandbox in TPMJS

Based on my thorough exploration of the codebase, here's a complete picture of how executors and sandbox work in the system:

---

### 1. **Prisma Schema Fields (Database Level)**

The agent model in `/packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma` (lines 608-677) includes:

```prisma
executorType         String?    @map("executor_type") @db.VarChar(50)
executorConfig       Json?      @map("executor_config") @db.JsonB
envVars              Json?      @map("env_vars") @db.JsonB
```

The **Collection** model (lines 484-558) has identical fields. This enables a **cascade hierarchy**: Agent → Collection → System Default.

---

### 2. **Type Definitions** (`packages/types/src/executor.ts`)

There are **three executor types**:

| Type | Use Case | Config Fields |
|------|----------|---------------|
| `default` | Stateless (Railway executor via package-executor) | None |
| `custom_url` | Custom HTTP executor endpoint | `url` (required), `apiKey` (optional) |
| `sandbox` | Stateful sessions with persistent filesystem | `url` (optional, falls back to `AGENT_SANDBOX_URL`), `apiKey` (optional) |

Key schemas:
- **ExecutorTypeSchema**: `z.enum(['default', 'custom_url', 'sandbox'])`
- **SandboxExecutorConfig**: Requires `sessionId` in execute requests (in addition to base `ExecuteToolRequest`)
- **ExecutorConfig**: Discriminated union that validates the shape based on type

---

### 3. **Executor Resolution Logic** (`apps/web/src/lib/executors/index.ts`)

**Core Functions:**

- **`parseExecutorConfig(executorType, executorConfig)`** (lines 83-119)
  - Safely parses database JSON to strongly-typed config
  - Returns `null` for invalid configs, default for 'default' type

- **`resolveExecutorConfig(agentConfig, collectionConfig)`** (lines 61-77)
  - **Cascade priority**: Agent (highest) → Collection (medium) → System default (lowest)
  - Non-null, non-'default' configs take precedence
  - Used during tool building to determine which executor each tool gets

- **`executeWithExecutor(config, request, sessionId?)`** (lines 432-470)
  - Routes to appropriate executor based on config type:
    - `sandbox` → calls `executeWithSandbox()` (requires `sessionId`)
    - `custom_url` → calls `executeWithCustomUrl()` 
    - `default` → calls `executePackage()` (stateless Railway executor)

**Sandbox-Specific Functions:**

- **`resolveSandboxUrl(config)`** (lines 200-202): Returns `config.url || process.env.AGENT_SANDBOX_URL || null`
- **`createSandboxSession(url, apiKey, sessionId, timeoutSeconds?)`** (lines 208-269): Idempotent session creation with retry logic
- **`executeWithSandbox(url, apiKey, request, sessionId, timeout?)`** (lines 313-422): Includes retry on 429/502/503 and network errors

---

### 4. **Tool Building** (`apps/web/src/lib/agents/build-tools.ts`)

**Key Function: `buildAgentTools(agent, callerEnvVars?, sessionId?)`** (lines 246-311)

**How it works:**

1. **Parses agent-level executor config** → applies to ALL tools
2. **For each collection in agent:**
   - Parses collection-level executor config
   - **Resolves config** (agent > collection > default)
   - Parses and **merges env vars** (collection base + agent overrides)
   - Builds tool definitions with resolved executor + merged env vars + sessionId
3. **For individual agent tools:**
   - Uses agent config or default (no collection context)
   - Uses only agent env vars (no collection merging)

**Sandbox Integration:**
- `sessionId` is passed through to `createToolDefinition()` 
- `createToolDefinition()` passes `sessionId` to `executeWithExecutor()` for sandbox requests

**Environment Variable Cascade:**
```javascript
// Collection env vars (base)
{ "API_KEY": "coll-key", "REGION": "us-east-1" }

// Agent env vars (overrides)
{ "API_KEY": "agent-key", "DEBUG": "true" }

// Result: Agent overrides collection for same keys, unique keys merged
{ "API_KEY": "agent-key", "REGION": "us-east-1", "DEBUG": "true" }
```

---

### 5. **Agent Creation/Editing** 

**At Creation Time** (`/api/agents` POST route):
- **NOTE:** `executorType` and `executorConfig` are **NOT** in `CreateAgentSchema` (lines 32-50 of `packages/types/src/agent.ts`)
- Agents are created with model config only, executor config comes later via updates

**At Update Time** (`UpdateAgentSchema`):
```typescript
executorType: ExecutorTypeSchema.nullable().optional(),
executorConfig: ExecutorConfigUpdateSchema,  // { url?, apiKey? }
envVars: z.record(z.string(), z.string()).nullable().optional(),
```

**In UI** (`/dashboard/agents/new/page.tsx`):
- New agent form only shows: name, uid, description, provider, model, systemPrompt, temperature, max tool calls, context messages
- **No executor configuration shown** at creation
- Users configure executor after creation (on agent details page - not provided in your search results, but likely exists)

---

### 6. **Conversation Execution Flow** (`/api/agents/[id]/conversation/[conversationId]` POST)

**Sandbox Setup** (lines 366-397):

```typescript
let sessionId: string | undefined;
if (agent.executorType === 'sandbox') {
  const sandboxConfig = parseExecutorConfig(agent.executorType, agent.executorConfig);
  if (sandboxConfig && sandboxConfig.type === 'sandbox') {
    const sandboxUrl = resolveSandboxUrl(sandboxConfig);
    if (!sandboxUrl) {
      // Error: AGENT_SANDBOX_URL not configured
    }
    sessionId = `${agent.id}:${conversationId}`;
    // Create/resume session before tool building
    await createSandboxSession(sandboxUrl, sandboxConfig.apiKey, sessionId);
  }
}

// Build tools with sessionId
const tools = buildAgentTools(agent, callerEnvVars, sessionId);
```

**Key Details:**
- Sandbox session is created/resumed **before** streaming begins
- sessionId format: `{agentId}:{conversationId}` (stable across multiple messages)
- Session creation is idempotent (extending TTL on subsequent calls)
- Every tool call includes `sessionId` in the executor request

---

### 7. **URL References in Codebase**

**Environment Variables:**
- **`AGENT_SANDBOX_URL`** (web app): Falls back URL when agent doesn't specify custom sandbox
  - Used in `resolveSandboxUrl()` at runtime
  - Documented in `/docs/executors/sandbox/page.tsx` (line 977)
  
- **`SANDBOX_EXECUTOR_URL`** (via `package-executor`): 
  - Not directly referenced in web app (abstracted in `@tpmjs/package-executor`)
  - This is the Railway executor endpoint used by default executor

**Configuration URLs:**
- Agent/Collection can specify custom URLs in `executorConfig.url`
- Sandbox: Optional (falls back to `AGENT_SANDBOX_URL` env var)
- Custom URL: Required

---

### 8. **Sandbox Documentation** (`/docs/executors/sandbox/page.tsx`)

Comprehensive guide showing:
- **Config cascade** (lines 245-255): Agent overrides Collection overrides Default
- **Session lifecycle**: Sessions persist for 1 hour by default, destroyed on conversation delete
- **Session endpoints**: POST/GET/DELETE `/sessions/{sessionId}`
- **Execute Tool API**: POST `/execute-tool` with `sessionId` parameter
- **Limits**: 100MB disk per session, 50 concurrent sessions, 1hr TTL
- **Environment variables**: `EXECUTOR_API_KEY`, `MAX_CONCURRENT_SESSIONS`, `DEFAULT_SESSION_TTL_SECONDS`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, etc.

---

### 9. **Workflow Diagram (from docs)**

```
User Message
    ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  TPMJS Web App (Next.js)            │
│  1. Create/resume sandbox session   │
│  2. Stream AI response              │
│  3. Route tool calls to sandbox     │
└──────────────┬──────────────────────┘
               │ POST /execute-tool
               │ { sessionId, params }
               ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Agent Sandbox Server (Deno)        │
│  Session: agent123:conv456          │
│  /workspace/ (persistent)           │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 10. **Key Architectural Insights**

1. **No executor config at agent creation** — only settable on updates
2. **Cascade resolution is per-tool** — different tools in same agent can come from different collections with different executors
3. **Session ID stability** — `agentId:conversationId` ensures same workspace across multiple message turns
4. **Idempotent session creation** — calling create again just extends TTL
5. **Environment variable isolation** — set per-execution, cleaned up afterward
6. **Fallback chain** — Agent config → Collection config → `AGENT_SANDBOX_URL` → error
7. **Retry resilience** — Sandbox executor retries on 429 (capacity), 502/503 (transient), and network errors

---

### Summary Table

| Concept | Where Stored | Where Used | Cascade? |
|---------|--------------|-----------|----------|
| `executorType` | Agent/Collection DB | Tool building, routing | Yes (Agent → Collection → Default) |
| `executorConfig` | Agent/Collection DB (JSON) | URL resolution, auth | Yes |
| `envVars` | Agent/Collection DB (JSON) | Tool execution | Yes (Agent overrides Collection) |
| `sessionId` | Not stored (computed) | Sandbox requests | Per conversation |
| `AGENT_SANDBOX_URL` | Env var | Fallback for sandbox URL | No (static) |
| `SANDBOX_EXECUTOR_URL` | Env var (in package-executor) | Default executor routing | No (static) |

This architecture enables flexible, hot-swappable executors while maintaining backward compatibility with the default stateless executor.

## Sandbox-Shell Tool Collection & Tool Integration Report

I've thoroughly explored the sandbox-shell tool collection and how tool collections are attached to agents. Here's the complete breakdown:

---

### 1. **Sandbox-Shell Package Structure**

**Location:** `/packages/tools/official/sandbox-shell/`

**Package Metadata** (`package.json`):
```json
{
  "name": "@tpmjs/official-sandbox-shell",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "description": "Shell execution, file I/O, and directory listing tools for the TPMJS Agent Sandbox",
  "keywords": ["sandbox", "shell", "git", "filesystem", "ai", "agent"],
  "tpmjs": {
    "category": "sandbox",
    "frameworks": ["vercel-ai"],
    "tools": [
      { "name": "shellExec", "description": "Execute shell commands in sandbox..." },
      { "name": "readFile", "description": "Read files from sandbox..." },
      { "name": "writeFile", "description": "Write/create files in sandbox..." },
      { "name": "listFiles", "description": "List files and directories..." }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Exported Tools** (`src/index.ts`):
1. **`shellExec`** - Execute shell commands with 30-300 second timeout, stdout/stderr capped at 100KB
2. **`readFile`** - Read files with 500KB truncation, symlink escape protection
3. **`writeFile`** - Create/overwrite files with auto-directory creation
4. **`listFiles`** - Recursive directory listing with configurable depth (max 1,000 entries)

All tools use Deno APIs (`Deno.Command`, `Deno.readTextFile`, `Deno.writeTextFile`, `Deno.readDir`) and receive a `_sandboxWorkDir` parameter injected by the sandbox server. All paths are validated to prevent escape attacks.

---

### 2. **DB Schema: Tool Collection Relationships**

**Three key junction tables connect agents to tools:**

#### **AgentCollection** (Many-to-Many: Agent ↔ Collection)
```prisma
model AgentCollection {
  id           String     @id
  agentId      String     @map("agent_id")
  agent        Agent      @relation(fields: [agentId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  collectionId String     @map("collection_id")
  collection   Collection @relation(fields: [collectionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  position     Int        @default(0)          // Ordering within agent
  addedAt      DateTime   @default(now())
  @@unique([agentId, collectionId])
}
```

#### **AgentTool** (Many-to-Many: Agent ↔ Tool - Direct Assignment)
```prisma
model AgentTool {
  id       String   @id
  agentId  String   @map("agent_id")
  agent    Agent    @relation(fields: [agentId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  toolId   String   @map("tool_id")
  tool     Tool     @relation(fields: [toolId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  position Int      @default(0)              // Ordering within agent
  addedAt  DateTime @default(now())
  @@unique([agentId, toolId])
}
```

#### **CollectionTool** (Many-to-Many: Collection ↔ Tool)
```prisma
model CollectionTool {
  id           String     @id
  collectionId String     @map("collection_id")
  collection   Collection @relation(fields: [collectionId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  toolId       String     @map("tool_id")
  tool         Tool       @relation(fields: [toolId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  position     Int        @default(0)        // Ordering within collection
  note         String?    @db.VarChar(500)   // Optional user notes
  addedAt      DateTime   @default(now())
  @@unique([collectionId, toolId])
}
```

**Key Executor Config Fields:**
- Both `Agent` and `Collection` have: `executorType`, `executorConfig` (JSON), `envVars` (JSON)
- Cascade resolution: **Agent executor → Collection executor → System default**
- Environment variable merge: **Agent env vars override Collection env vars**

---

### 3. **How Tools Get Wired into AI SDK `streamText`**

**Flow in `buildAgentTools.ts`:**

```
1. fetchAgentWithTools(agentId)
   └─> Load agent with all relations:
       ├─ agent.collections[] (AgentCollection)
       │  └─ collection.tools[] (CollectionTool)
       │     └─ tool.package (Package metadata)
       └─ agent.tools[] (AgentTool)
          └─ tool.package (Package metadata)

2. buildAgentTools(agent, callerEnvVars?, sessionId?)
   └─ Iterate collections first, then individual tools
      For each tool:
        ├─ Parse collection executor config
        ├─ Resolve: agentConfig → collectionConfig → default
        ├─ Merge env vars: collectionEnvVars + agentEnvVars
        ├─ Deduplicate by `${npmPackageName}::${toolName}`
        └─ Call createToolDefinition(tool, resolvedConfig, mergedEnvVars, sessionId)

3. createToolDefinition(tool, config, envVars, sessionId)
   ├─ Create AI SDK tool with:
   │  ├─ description (from Tool record)
   │  ├─ inputSchema (full JSON Schema or legacy parameters array)
   │  └─ execute() async function
   │     └─ Call executeWithExecutor(config, request, sessionId)
   │        ├─ If config.type === 'sandbox': POST /execute-tool to sandbox URL with sessionId
   │        ├─ If config.type === 'custom_url': POST /execute-tool to custom URL
   │        └─ If config.type === 'default': Use @tpmjs/package-executor (Railway-based)
   └─ Return tools map keyed by sanitized name: "${npmPackageName}-${toolName}"

4. Tools passed to AI SDK's streamText()
   └─ Model uses tools to decide which to call and with what parameters
```

**Input Schema Hierarchy:**
1. **Preferred:** `tool.inputSchema` (full JSON Schema) - preserves nested objects/arrays
2. **Fallback:** `tool.parameters` array (legacy) - converted to Zod schema

---

### 4. **Executor Types in `@tpmjs/types/executor.ts`**

```typescript
enum ExecutorType = 'default' | 'custom_url' | 'sandbox'

// Executor Config Schema (Zod discriminated union)
{
  // 1. Default executor (Railway-hosted TPMJS executor)
  type: 'default'
  
  // 2. Custom URL executor
  type: 'custom_url'
  url: string (HTTPS required in production)
  apiKey?: string (Bearer token for /execute-tool endpoint)
  
  // 3. Sandbox executor (persistent sessions)
  type: 'sandbox'
  url?: string (falls back to AGENT_SANDBOX_URL env var)
  apiKey?: string (Bearer token for /execute-tool endpoint)
}

// Executor API Contracts
ExecuteToolRequest {
  packageName: string           // "@tpmjs/official-sandbox-shell"
  name: string                  // "shellExec"
  version?: string              // "0.1.0" or "latest"
  importUrl?: string            // Direct ESM.sh override
  params: Record<string, unknown>
  env?: Record<string, string>  // Injected environment variables
  // Sandbox-specific:
  sessionId?: string            // "agentId:conversationId"
}

ExecuteToolResponse {
  success: boolean
  output?: unknown              // Tool result
  error?: string                // Error message on failure
  executionTimeMs: number
}

// Sandbox Session Management
CreateSessionRequest/Response, DestroySessionResponse, SessionStatusResponse
```

**Session Creation (Sandbox):**
```typescript
POST /sessions
{
  sessionId: "agent123:conv456",
  timeoutSeconds?: 3600  // default 1 hour
}
→ Creates /workspace/ directory with persistent filesystem
```

---

### 5. **Sandbox Executor Docs Page Features**

**Location:** `/apps/web/src/app/docs/executors/sandbox/page.tsx`

**Documentation Structure:**
- **Overview:** Architecture diagram, when to use, multi-step workflows
- **Shell Tools:** Parameters, examples, response formats for all 4 tools
- **Sessions:** Lifecycle, TTL extension, orphan cleanup, session API endpoints
- **Executor Config:** Cascade resolution, TPMJS default vs self-hosted comparison
- **Environment Variables:** Server-side (EXECUTOR_API_KEY, MAX_CONCURRENT_SESSIONS, SESSION_DISK_QUOTA_MB) and agent-level env vars
- **Git Integration:** Public/private repo support via credential helper
- **Deployment:** Railway and Docker setup with environment variable configuration
- **Security:** Path sandboxing, process isolation (non-root deno user), timeout protection
- **Limits & Quotas:** Per-session 100MB disk, 50 concurrent sessions, 1-hour TTL, 30s-5min command timeout, 100KB output truncation
- **Execute Tool API:** Request/response format with field documentation
- **Health & Metrics:** `/health` and `/metrics` endpoints for monitoring

---

### 6. **Key Integration Points**

| Component | Role |
|-----------|------|
| `buildAgentTools.ts` | Orchestrates tool collection → AI SDK conversion |
| `tool-executor-agent.ts` | Creates AI SDK v6 tool definitions with `execute()` handlers |
| `executors/index.ts` | Routes execution to default/custom/sandbox executors with retry logic |
| `AgentCollection` | Links agents to curated tool collections with executor config override |
| `AgentTool` | Direct tool assignment to agents (individual tools) |
| `CollectionTool` | Tools within a collection (grouped by curator) |
| Sandbox docs | User-facing documentation for sandbox-only features |

---

### 7. **Executor Config Cascade Example**

```typescript
// Resolution priority (highest to lowest):
1. Agent.executorType + Agent.executorConfig
   → Applied to ALL tools (from collections + individual)

2. Collection.executorType + Collection.executorConfig
   → Applied to tools within that collection only
   → Overridden by Agent executor if agent has one

3. System default { type: 'default' }
   → Uses TPMJS Railway executor

// Environment variable merge:
Collection.envVars = { "API_KEY": "coll-key", "REGION": "us-east-1" }
Agent.envVars = { "API_KEY": "agent-key", "DEBUG": "true" }
Result = { "API_KEY": "agent-key", "REGION": "us-east-1", "DEBUG": "true" }
```

---

This architecture enables agents to use different executor backends seamlessly—from stateless default execution to persistent sandbox sessions with Git/file capabilities—while maintaining type safety and deduplication across overlapping tool sources.

```typescript
  name: string                  // "shellExec"
  version?: string              // "0.1.0" or "latest"
  importUrl?: string            // Direct ESM.sh override
  params: Record<string, unknown>
  env?: Record<string, string>  // Injected environment variables
  // Sandbox-specific:
  sessionId?: string            // "agentId:conversationId"
}

ExecuteToolResponse {
  success: boolean
  output?: unknown              // Tool result
  error?: string                // Error message on failure
  executionTimeMs: number
}

// Sandbox Session Management
CreateSessionRequest/Response, DestroySessionResponse, SessionStatusResponse
```

**Session Creation (Sandbox):**
```typescript
POST /sessions
{
  sessionId: "agent123:conv456",
  timeoutSeconds?: 3600  // default 1 hour
}
→ Creates /workspace/ directory with persistent filesystem
```

---

### 5. **Sandbox Executor Docs Page Features**

**Location:** `/apps/web/src/app/docs/executors/sandbox/page.tsx`

**Documentation Structure:**
- **Overview:** Architecture diagram, when to use, multi-step workflows
- **Shell Tools:** Parameters, examples, response formats for all 4 tools
- **Sessions:** Lifecycle, TTL extension, orphan cleanup, session API endpoints
- **Executor Config:** Cascade resolution, TPMJS default vs self-hosted comparison
- **Environment Variables:** Server-side (EXECUTOR_API_KEY, MAX_CONCURRENT_SESSIONS, SESSION_DISK_QUOTA_MB) and agent-level env vars
- **Git Integration:** Public/private repo support via credential helper
- **Deployment:** Railway and Docker setup with environment variable configuration
- **Security:** Path sandboxing, process isolation (non-root deno user), timeout protection
- **Limits & Quotas:** Per-session 100MB disk, 50 concurrent sessions, 1-hour TTL, 30s-5min command timeout, 100KB output truncation
- **Execute Tool API:** Request/response format with field documentation
- **Health & Metrics:** `/health` and `/metrics` endpoints for monitoring

---

### 6. **Key Integration Points**

| Component | Role |
|-----------|------|
| `buildAgentTools.ts` | Orchestrates tool collection → AI SDK conversion |
| `tool-executor-agent.ts` | Creates AI SDK v6 tool definitions with `execute()` handlers |
| `executors/index.ts` | Routes execution to default/custom/sandbox executors with retry logic |
| `AgentCollection` | Links agents to curated tool collections with executor config override |
| `AgentTool` | Direct tool assignment to agents (individual tools) |
| `CollectionTool` | Tools within a collection (grouped by curator) |
| Sandbox docs | User-facing documentation for sandbox-only features |

---

### 7. **Executor Config Cascade Example**

```typescript
// Resolution priority (highest to lowest):
1. Agent.executorType + Agent.executorConfig
   → Applied to ALL tools (from collections + individual)

2. Collection.executorType + Collection.executorConfig
   → Applied to tools within that collection only
   → Overridden by Agent executor if agent has one

3. System default { type: 'default' }
   → Uses TPMJS Railway executor

// Environment variable merge:
Collection.envVars = { "API_KEY": "coll-key", "REGION": "us-east-1" }
Agent.envVars = { "API_KEY": "agent-key", "DEBUG": "true" }
Result = { "API_KEY": "agent-key", "REGION": "us-east-1", "DEBUG": "true" }
```

---

This architecture enables agents to use different executor backends seamlessly—from stateless default execution to persistent sandbox sessions with Git/file capabilities—while maintaining type safety and deduplication across overlapping tool sources.

Now I have a thorough understanding of the architecture. Let me think about what the user wants:

**Current state:**
- `executor_type` can be `'default'`, `'custom_url'`, or `'sandbox'`
- Sandbox is treated as an executor type, meaning an agent's executor is either default, custom URL, OR sandbox
- This means you can't have a custom executor AND a sandbox at the same time

**User's vision:**
- Custom executors and sandboxes are two different things
- "Users should just be able to boot up a sandbox during their normal existing agent chats"
- This means sandbox should be an independent feature, not an executor type


- The real value of sandbox comes from the sandbox-shell tools (shellExec, readFile, writeFile, listFiles) that provide a persistent workspace
- So the fix is to decouple these concepts: executors handle where tools run (default or custom), while sandbox becomes a separate toggle that grants access to sandbox-shell tools and maintains a persistent session
- Regular tools still route through whatever executor is configured, but sandbox-shell tools always go to the sandbox server
- I need to figure out how to identify which tools are sandbox-specific so they can be routed correctly
- The simplest approach is probably just a `sandboxEnabled` boolean on the Agent that users can toggle, which automatically creates a sandbox session when needed and injects the sandbox-shell tools without requiring manual setup
- I'd add a `sandboxConfig` field to store any additional sandbox settings, keeping the executor configuration straightforward with just `'default'` or `'custom_url'` options
- Defining the schema... Looking at how `buildAgentTools` currently works, I see it resolves executor config at both the agent and collection level, then merges them together. But with sandboxes, I need to handle routing differently — sandbox tools should go to the sandbox server regardless of the executor config, while everything else respects the agent or collection's executor settings. I'm thinking through how to identify which tools should use the sandbox executor—the cleanest approach would be to let the sandbox-shell collection itself declare `executorType = 'sandbox'` at the collection level, so the agent's executor config only needs to handle `'default'` or `'custom_url'` for regular tools.

But that creates a cascade problem: if the agent's executor config overrides the collection's, sandbox tools would get routed incorrectly. So I'm reconsidering the whole approach—maybe sandbox should just be a separate `sandboxEnabled` boolean on the agent that automatically injects sandbox-shell tools and creates a sandbox session at conversation start, keeping it independent from the executor routing logic.

This means removing `'sandbox'` from the executor type enum, adding `sandboxEnabled` and optionally `sandboxUrl` to the Agent model, and handling sandbox tool injection separately in `buildAgentTools` rather than through the executor cascade. Now I'm thinking through the database schema changes needed.

I'll add a `sandbox_enabled` boolean field to the Agent model and optionally a `sandbox_url` field for custom sandbox servers, since most agents will use the default `AGENT_SANDBOX_URL`. For the UI, I should add a toggle in agent settings to enable the sandbox with a description about the persistent workspace and available tools.

The trickier part is the API key authentication—the sandbox server needs a way to verify requests from agents. I'm thinking the setup would be a single `EXECUTOR_API_KEY` environment variable on the sandbox server that all agents use, with `AGENT_SANDBOX_URL` pointing to the sandbox endpoint. For self-hosted sandboxes, they'd configure their own authentication mechanism.

To keep this simple initially, I'll just add the `sandbox_enabled` boolean to the schema and pull the sandbox URL and API key from environment variables, leaving room for advanced users to customize later.

Perfect! I now have a comprehensive view of the agent settings/edit UI components. Let me compile this for you:

## Agent Settings/Edit UI Components - Complete Overview

### 1. **Agent Detail/Edit Page**
**File:** `/Users/ajaxdavis/repos/tpmjs/tpmjs/apps/web/src/app/dashboard/agents/[id]/page.tsx`

This is the main agent configuration page with **5 tabs**:

#### Tab 1: **Tools** (lines 1175-1284)
- Search interface to find and add tools to the agent
- Table displaying attached tools with removal button
- Live search with debouncing (300ms)
- Limits enforced: `MAX_TOOLS_PER_AGENT: 50`
- API endpoints: `POST /api/agents/[id]/tools`, `DELETE /api/agents/[id]/tools/[toolId]`

#### Tab 2: **Collections** (lines 1287-1397)
- Search interface to find and add tool collections
- Table displaying attached collections (shows tool count per collection)
- Collections are groups of tools - can add up to 10 per agent
- Limits enforced: `MAX_COLLECTIONS_PER_AGENT: 10`
- API endpoints: `POST /api/agents/[id]/collections`, `DELETE /api/agents/[id]/collections/[collectionId]`

#### Tab 3: **API** (line 1401)
- API documentation and code examples
- Shows all available endpoints with request/response examples
- Language switcher (cURL, TypeScript, Python)
- Authentication details and conversation management examples

#### Tab 4: **Env Vars** (lines 1404-1431)
- Uses `<EnvVarsEditor />` component
- Allows setting environment variables passed to tools at runtime
- Agent vars override collection vars
- Auto-saves changes
- Features: Add/remove/update vars, paste .env snippets

#### Tab 5: **Settings** (lines 1435-1600)
Main configuration settings:
- **Agent Details**: Name, UID, Description
- **Model Config**: Provider dropdown (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq, Mistral) with model selection
- **System Prompt**: Long textarea (max 10,000 chars)
- **Behavior Parameters**:
  - Temperature (0-2, default 0.7)
  - Max Tool Calls Per Turn (1-100, default 20)
  - Max Messages In Context (1-100, default 10)
- **Public Visibility Toggle**: Switch to make agent publicly discoverable
- **Executor Configuration Panel** (see below)
- **Danger Zone**: Delete agent button

---

### 2. **Executor Configuration Component**
**File:** `/Users/ajaxdavis/repos/tpmjs/tpmjs/apps/web/src/components/ExecutorConfigPanel.tsx`

Allows users to toggle executor type with three options:

**Three Executor Types:**
1. **TPMJS Default** (type: 'default')
   - Free, managed executor hosted by TPMJS
   - No configuration needed

2. **Custom Executor** (type: 'custom_url')
   - Self-hosted on your infrastructure
   - Required fields: URL
   - Optional: API Key for authentication
   - Includes "Verify Connection" button

3. **Agent Sandbox** (type: 'sandbox')
   - Stateful execution with persistent filesystem
   - Optional: Sandbox URL (defaults to TPMJS)
   - Optional: API Key for authentication
   - Badge shows "Stateful" capability

**Verification Feature:**
- `POST /api/executors/verify` endpoint
- Tests health check and execution
- Returns verification result with health status and execution time

---

### 3. **Environment Variables Editor Component**
**File:** `/Users/ajaxdavis/repos/tpmjs/tpmjs/apps/web/src/components/EnvVarsEditor.tsx`

Reusable editor with features:
- Add/edit/remove environment variables
- Paste .env file snippets with parsing
- Auto-capitalization of keys
- Password masking for values
- Diff detection to prevent unnecessary updates
- Fire-and-forget saves

---

### 4. **Agent Update API Route**
**File:** `/Users/ajaxdavis/repos/tpmjs/tpmjs/apps/web/src/app/api/agents/[id]/route.ts`

**PATCH /api/agents/[id]** - Updates agent configuration

**Updatable Fields** (from `UpdateAgentSchema`):
```typescript
{
  name: string (1-100 chars) - optional
  uid: string (1-50 chars, alphanumeric + hyphens) - optional
  description: string | null (max 500 chars) - optional
  provider: 'OPENAI' | 'ANTHROPIC' | 'GOOGLE' | 'GROQ' | 'MISTRAL' - optional
  modelId: string - optional
  systemPrompt: string | null (max 10,000 chars) - optional
  temperature: number (0-2) - optional
  maxToolCallsPerTurn: number (1-100) - optional
  maxMessagesInContext: number (1-100) - optional
  isPublic: boolean - optional
  executorType: 'default' | 'custom_url' | 'sandbox' | null - optional
  executorConfig: { url: string, apiKey?: string } | null - optional
  envVars: Record<string, string> | null - optional
}
```

**Validation:**
- UID uniqueness (per user, for updates)
- Name uniqueness (per user, for updates)
- JSON field transformation (null → Prisma.JsonNull)
- Activity logging with type detection (CONFIG_UPDATED vs UPDATED)

**Returns:**
- Updated agent object with tool/collection counts
- Uses `_count` pagination optimization

---

### 5. **Tool Management API Routes**

**GET /api/agents/[id]/tools** - List tools
- Returns: Array of tool objects with npm package names
- Ordered by position (ASC)

**POST /api/agents/[id]/tools** - Add a tool
- Schema: `AddToolToAgentSchema` with toolId and optional position
- Validations:
  - Agent ownership check
  - Tool limit check (MAX: 50)
  - Tool existence validation
  - Duplicate prevention
  - Activity logging with tool name

**DELETE /api/agents/[id]/tools/[toolId]** - Remove a tool
- Simple removal of agent-tool link
- Activity logging with tool name

---

### 6. **Collection Management API Routes**

**GET /api/agents/[id]/collections** - List collections
- Returns: Array of collection objects with tool counts
- Ordered by position (ASC)

**POST /api/agents/[id]/collections** - Add a collection
- Schema: `AddCollectionToAgentSchema` with collectionId and optional position
- Validations:
  - Agent ownership check
  - Collection limit check (MAX: 10)
  - Collection existence and access check
  - Duplicate prevention
  - Activity logging with collection name

**DELETE /api/agents/[id]/collections/[collectionId]** - Remove a collection
- Simple removal of agent-collection link
- Activity logging with collection name

---

### 7. **Key UI Features**

**Status Badges** (line 1161-1169):
- Shows "Public" or "Private" badge
- "Custom Executor" badge if using custom URL executor
- "Agent Sandbox" badge if using sandbox executor

**Search with Debouncing**:
- Tools: 300ms debounce, filters already-attached items
- Collections: 300ms debounce, filters already-attached items
- Click-outside detection to close search dropdowns

**Toggles:**
- Public visibility switch with explanation text
- Three executor type buttons with descriptions

**Form Structure:**
- Grouped by section with fieldsets and legends
- Color-coded status badges
- Danger zone with confirmation dialogs

---

### 8. **Limits & Constraints**

From `/packages/types/src/agent.ts`:
```typescript
AGENT_LIMITS = {
  MAX_AGENTS_PER_USER: 20
  MAX_COLLECTIONS_PER_AGENT: 10
  MAX_TOOLS_PER_AGENT: 50
  MAX_SYSTEM_PROMPT_LENGTH: 10,000
  MAX_NAME_LENGTH: 100
  MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH: 500
  MAX_UID_LENGTH: 50
}
```

All limits are enforced both client-side and server-side (API validation).

---

### Summary

The agent settings UI is a comprehensive **single-page dashboard** with:
- **5 organized tabs** for different concerns
- **Two-way syncing** with API (debounced saves)
- **Real-time search** with duplicate prevention
- **Executor flexibility** (3 modes)
- **Feature toggles** via switches and radio buttons
- **Activity logging** for all major changes
- **Comprehensive validation** with user-friendly errors

```typescript
  temperature: number (0-2) - optional
  maxToolCallsPerTurn: number (1-100) - optional
  maxMessagesInContext: number (1-100) - optional
  isPublic: boolean - optional
  executorType: 'default' | 'custom_url' | 'sandbox' | null - optional
  executorConfig: { url: string, apiKey?: string } | null - optional
  envVars: Record<string, string> | null - optional
}
```

**Validation:**
- UID uniqueness (per user, for updates)
- Name uniqueness (per user, for updates)
- JSON field transformation (null → Prisma.JsonNull)
- Activity logging with type detection (CONFIG_UPDATED vs UPDATED)

**Returns:**
- Updated agent object with tool/collection counts
- Uses `_count` pagination optimization

---

### 5. **Tool Management API Routes**

**GET /api/agents/[id]/tools** - List tools
- Returns: Array of tool objects with npm package names
- Ordered by position (ASC)

**POST /api/agents/[id]/tools** - Add a tool
- Schema: `AddToolToAgentSchema` with toolId and optional position
- Validations:
  - Agent ownership check
  - Tool limit check (MAX: 50)
  - Tool existence validation
  - Duplicate prevention
  - Activity logging with tool name

**DELETE /api/agents/[id]/tools/[toolId]** - Remove a tool
- Simple removal of agent-tool link
- Activity logging with tool name

---

### 6. **Collection Management API Routes**

**GET /api/agents/[id]/collections** - List collections
- Returns: Array of collection objects with tool counts
- Ordered by position (ASC)

**POST /api/agents/[id]/collections** - Add a collection
- Schema: `AddCollectionToAgentSchema` with collectionId and optional position
- Validations:
  - Agent ownership check
  - Collection limit check (MAX: 10)
  - Collection existence and access check
  - Duplicate prevention
  - Activity logging with collection name

**DELETE /api/agents/[id]/collections/[collectionId]** - Remove a collection
- Simple removal of agent-collection link
- Activity logging with collection name

---

### 7. **Key UI Features**

**Status Badges** (line 1161-1169):
- Shows "Public" or "Private" badge
- "Custom Executor" badge if using custom URL executor
- "Agent Sandbox" badge if using sandbox executor

**Search with Debouncing**:
- Tools: 300ms debounce, filters already-attached items
- Collections: 300ms debounce, filters already-attached items
- Click-outside detection to close search dropdowns

**Toggles:**
- Public visibility switch with explanation text
- Three executor type buttons with descriptions

**Form Structure:**
- Grouped by section with fieldsets and legends
- Color-coded status badges
- Danger zone with confirmation dialogs

---

### 8. **Limits & Constraints**

From `/packages/types/src/agent.ts`:
```typescript
AGENT_LIMITS = {
  MAX_AGENTS_PER_USER: 20
  MAX_COLLECTIONS_PER_AGENT: 10
  MAX_TOOLS_PER_AGENT: 50
  MAX_SYSTEM_PROMPT_LENGTH: 10,000
  MAX_NAME_LENGTH: 100
  MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH: 500
  MAX_UID_LENGTH: 50
}
```

All limits are enforced both client-side and server-side (API validation).

---

### Summary

The agent settings UI is a comprehensive **single-page dashboard** with:
- **5 organized tabs** for different concerns
- **Two-way syncing** with API (debounced saves)
- **Real-time search** with duplicate prevention
- **Executor flexibility** (3 modes)
- **Feature toggles** via switches and radio buttons
- **Activity logging** for all major changes
- **Comprehensive validation** with user-friendly errors

Only sandbox-shell tools should hit the sandbox server — regular tools need their own executor path. So I need to pass both the regular executor config and sandbox config through the tool building process, then route each tool appropriately based on its source.

But then there's the question of how to identify which tools are sandbox tools. The package name gives us a hint, but users might create their own sandbox-compatible tools too. The real distinction the user wants is that custom executors and sandboxes are separate concerns — a sandbox is a workspace with shell capabilities, while a custom executor is just where regular tools run.

So the sandbox-shell tools are the actual sandbox implementation. When sandbox mode is enabled, a session gets created automatically and those four built-in tools become available to execute against the sandbox server, while everything else still uses the configured executor. The user doesn't need to manually add the sandbox collection since it's injected automatically when the toggle is on. Looking at how the sandbox URL is already resolved from environment variables, I should follow the same pattern for the API key by adding an `AGENT_SANDBOX_API_KEY` env var that gets used as a fallback, similar to how `AGENT_SANDBOX_URL` works.

# Separate Sandbox from Custom Executors

## Context

Currently, "sandbox" is one of three executor types (`default | custom_url | sandbox`). This conflates two independent concepts:

- **Executor** = Where tools run (TPMJS default infrastructure, or a user's own server)
- **Sandbox** = A persistent workspace with shell, file, and git tools

A user can't have a custom executor AND a sandbox. The user wants these separated so any agent can "boot up a sandbox" during normal chats — just flip a toggle.

## Design

- Remove `'sandbox'` from executor types. Executors become: `default | custom_url`
- Add `sandboxEnabled` boolean to the Agent model
- When sandbox is enabled, 4 sandbox tools (shellExec, readFile, writeFile, listFiles) are **auto-injected** — no need to manually add a tool collection
- Sandbox tools route to the sandbox server; all other tools route to the configured executor (default/custom_url)
- Sandbox URL + API key come from env vars (`AGENT_SANDBOX_URL`, `AGENT_SANDBOX_API_KEY`)

## Files to Modify

### 1. Prisma Schema — `packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma`

Add to Agent model (after `envVars` field, line ~647):
```prisma
sandboxEnabled       Boolean    @default(false) @map("sandbox_enabled")
```

### 2. Types — `packages/types/src/executor.ts`

- Remove `'sandbox'` from `ExecutorTypeSchema`: `z.enum(['default', 'custom_url'])`
- Remove `SandboxExecutorConfigSchema` from the `ExecutorConfigSchema` discriminated union
- Delete the `SandboxExecutorConfig` type export
- Keep ALL sandbox session types (`CreateSessionRequest/Response`, `DestroySessionResponse`, `SessionStatusResponse`, `SandboxExecuteToolRequest`) — these are still used internally

### 3. Types — `packages/types/src/agent.ts`

- Add to `UpdateAgentSchema`: `sandboxEnabled: z.boolean().optional()`
- Add to `CreateAgentSchema`: `sandboxEnabled: z.boolean().default(false).optional()`

### 4. Executor Logic — `apps/web/src/lib/executors/index.ts`

- Remove `'sandbox'` case from `parseExecutorConfig()` (lines 106-118)
- Remove `'sandbox'` routing from `executeWithExecutor()` (lines 444-456)
- Keep `resolveSandboxUrl()`, `createSandboxSession()`, `destroySandboxSession()`, `executeWithSandbox()` — but change `resolveSandboxUrl` to read only from env var:
  ```typescript
  export function getSandboxConfig(): { url: string | null; apiKey: string | undefined } {
    return {
      url: process.env.AGENT_SANDBOX_URL || null,
      apiKey: process.env.AGENT_SANDBOX_API_KEY || undefined,
    };
  }
  ```
- Update `getExecutorDescription()` to remove sandbox case

### 5. Tool Building — `apps/web/src/lib/agents/build-tools.ts`

Add a new function `injectSandboxTools()` that creates 4 hard-coded tool definitions:

```typescript
const SANDBOX_PACKAGE = '@tpmjs/official-sandbox-shell';
const SANDBOX_VERSION = '0.1.0';

const SANDBOX_TOOL_DEFS = [
  {
    name: 'shellExec',
    description: 'Execute a shell command in the sandbox workspace. Supports any shell command including git, npm, curl, etc. Commands run in a persistent workspace directory.',
    schema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        command: { type: 'string', description: 'Shell command to execute' },
        timeout: { type: 'number', description: 'Timeout in milliseconds (default: 30000, max: 300000)' },
      },
      required: ['command'],
      additionalProperties: false,
    },
  },
  {
    name: 'readFile',
    description: 'Read a file from the sandbox workspace. Returns the file content as a string.',
    schema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        path: { type: 'string', description: 'File path relative to workspace root' },
      },
      required: ['path'],
      additionalProperties: false,
    },
  },
  {
    name: 'writeFile',
    description: 'Write or create a file in the sandbox workspace.',
    schema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        path: { type: 'string', description: 'File path relative to workspace root' },
        content: { type: 'string', description: 'File content to write' },
        createDirs: { type: 'boolean', description: 'Auto-create parent directories if needed' },
      },
      required: ['path', 'content'],
      additionalProperties: false,
    },
  },
  {
    name: 'listFiles',
    description: 'List files and directories in the sandbox workspace.',
    schema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        path: { type: 'string', description: 'Directory path relative to workspace root (default: root)' },
        recursive: { type: 'boolean', description: 'List files recursively' },
        maxDepth: { type: 'number', description: 'Maximum recursion depth (default: 5, max: 10)' },
      },
      additionalProperties: false,
    },
  },
];
```

Each tool gets wrapped with an execute function that calls `executeWithSandbox(sandboxUrl, apiKey, request, sessionId)` directly — bypassing the normal executor resolution.

In `buildAgentTools()`: if `sessionId` is provided, call `injectSandboxTools()` first. Sandbox tool keys are added to `seenTools` set so they won't be duplicated if the user also has the sandbox-shell collection attached.

### 6. Conversation Routes (both versions)

**`apps/web/src/app/api/[username]/agents/[agentSlug]/conversation/[conversationId]/route.ts`**
**`apps/web/src/app/api/agents/[id]/conversation/[conversationId]/route.ts`**

POST handler — change sandbox session setup:
```typescript
// Before: if (agent.executorType === 'sandbox')
// After:
if (agent.sandboxEnabled) {
  const { url: sandboxUrl, apiKey: sandboxApiKey } = getSandboxConfig();
  if (!sandboxUrl) {
    return error 502 "Sandbox URL not configured..."
  }
  sessionId = `${agent.id}:${conversationId}`;
  await createSandboxSession(sandboxUrl, sandboxApiKey, sessionId);
}
```

DELETE handler — change sandbox cleanup:
```typescript
// Before: if (agent.executorType === 'sandbox')
// After:
if (agent.sandboxEnabled) {
  const { url: sandboxUrl, apiKey: sandboxApiKey } = getSandboxConfig();
  if (sandboxUrl) {
    destroySandboxSession(sandboxUrl, sandboxApiKey, sessionId).catch(() => {});
  }
}
```

Also update the `select` clauses to include `sandboxEnabled` instead of `executorType`/`executorConfig` where those were only used for sandbox checks.

### 7. ExecutorConfigPanel — `apps/web/src/components/ExecutorConfigPanel.tsx`

- Remove the "Agent Sandbox" radio button entirely
- Remove `'sandbox'` from `ExecutorTypeOption` type: `'default' | 'custom_url'`
- Remove sandbox-specific URL/API key helper text
- Clean up `getInitialType`, `getInitialUrl`, `getInitialApiKey` to remove sandbox cases

### 8. New Component — `apps/web/src/components/SandboxToggle.tsx`

Simple toggle component for the agent settings page:
```typescript
interface SandboxToggleProps {
  enabled: boolean;
  onChange: (enabled: boolean) => void;
  disabled?: boolean;
}
```

Shows a switch with description: "Enable a persistent workspace with shell, file, and git tools. Your agent can execute commands, read/write files, and clone repositories."

### 9. Agent Detail Page — `apps/web/src/app/dashboard/agents/[id]/page.tsx`

- Add `<SandboxToggle>` to Settings tab (above or below the executor config panel)
- Update status badges: show "Sandbox" badge based on `agent.sandboxEnabled` instead of `agent.executorType === 'sandbox'`
- Wire `sandboxEnabled` into the PATCH request on save

### 10. Agent Update API — `apps/web/src/app/api/agents/[id]/route.ts`

- Handle `sandboxEnabled` field in the PATCH handler (pass through to Prisma update)

### 11. Agent Clone API — `apps/web/src/app/api/agents/[id]/clone/route.ts`

- Copy `sandboxEnabled` from source agent to clone (it's a simple boolean, safe to copy)

### 12. Data Migration

After schema migration, run:
```sql
-- Move sandbox agents to new model
UPDATE agents SET sandbox_enabled = true WHERE executor_type = 'sandbox';
UPDATE agents SET executor_type = NULL, executor_config = NULL WHERE executor_type = 'sandbox';
```

### 13. Docs Page — `apps/web/src/app/docs/executors/sandbox/page.tsx`

Update to reflect sandbox as a separate toggle, not an executor type. Remove references to `executorType: 'sandbox'`.

### 14. Integration Tests

Update test helpers and any tests that reference `executorType === 'sandbox'` to use `sandboxEnabled` instead. The sandbox-direct tests (sandbox-health, sandbox-sessions, etc.) are unaffected since they test the sandbox server directly.

## Implementation Order

1. `packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma` — add field
2. Run `pnpm --filter=@tpmjs/db db:generate` + `db:push`
3. `packages/types/src/executor.ts` — remove sandbox from executor types
4. `packages/types/src/agent.ts` — add sandboxEnabled
5. `apps/web/src/lib/executors/index.ts` — add `getSandboxConfig()`, remove sandbox from executor routing
6. `apps/web/src/lib/agents/build-tools.ts` — add `injectSandboxTools()`
7. Both conversation routes — switch to `agent.sandboxEnabled`
8. `apps/web/src/components/ExecutorConfigPanel.tsx` — remove sandbox option
9. `apps/web/src/components/SandboxToggle.tsx` — new component
10. `apps/web/src/app/dashboard/agents/[id]/page.tsx` — add toggle, update badges
11. `apps/web/src/app/api/agents/[id]/route.ts` — handle sandboxEnabled in PATCH
12. `apps/web/src/app/api/agents/[id]/clone/route.ts` — copy sandboxEnabled
13. Data migration SQL
14. Type-check + test

## Verification

1. `pnpm --filter=@tpmjs/db db:generate` — regenerate Prisma client
2. `pnpm --filter=@tpmjs/db db:push` — push schema to dev DB
3. `pnpm type-check` — full monorepo type check
4. Build sandbox Docker: `docker build -t tpmjs-sandbox:test templates/agent-sandbox/`
5. Run sandbox container: `docker run -d --name sb -p 3002:3002 -e EXECUTOR_API_KEY=dev tpmjs-sandbox:test`
6. Run integration tests:
   ```bash
   INTEGRATION_TESTS=true SANDBOX_TEST_URL=http://localhost:3002 SANDBOX_TEST_API_KEY=dev \
   TEST_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3000 INTEGRATION_TEST_SESSION_TOKEN=dummy INTEGRATION_TEST_API_KEY=dummy \
   pnpm --filter=@tpmjs/web vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.mjs src/test/integration/sandbox/
   ```
7. Start dev server, toggle sandbox on for an agent, verify tools appear in chat
8. `docker rm -f sb`

## Context

The Agent Sandbox server and shell tools are fully implemented. We need integration tests that:
1. **Layer 1**: Test the sandbox server directly via its HTTP API (Docker container in CI)
2. **Layer 2**: Run the existing E2E test through the TPMJS web app (already written, just needs CI wiring)

## Files to Create

### Helper files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `apps/web/src/test/integration/sandbox/_helpers/sandbox-client.ts` | HTTP client for sandbox server API (health, metrics, sessions, execute-tool, raw requests) |
| `apps/web/src/test/integration/sandbox/_helpers/sandbox-context.ts` | Test context: configures client from env vars, tracks sessions for cleanup, `isSandboxAvailable()` gate |

### Test files (Layer 1 — direct sandbox API)

| File | Tests |
|------|-------|
| `sandbox-health.integration.test.ts` | `GET /health` shape, `GET /metrics` shape, response time |
| `sandbox-sessions.integration.test.ts` | Create, get, resume (idempotent), destroy, 404 on missing, missing sessionId → 400, custom TTL |
| `sandbox-tools.integration.test.ts` | shellExec (echo, exit code, timeout), writeFile+readFile round-trip, createDirs, listFiles root + recursive |
| `sandbox-security.integration.test.ts` | Path traversal `../` blocked for readFile/writeFile, symlink escape blocked, auth 401 when key required, health/metrics allow unauthenticated |
| `sandbox-isolation.integration.test.ts` | Two sessions have separate workspaces, git clone public repo, git init + commit |
| `sandbox-quota.integration.test.ts` | Fill workspace beyond quota → next tool call rejected |

### CI workflow

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `.github/workflows/sandbox-tests.yml` | Two-job workflow: `sandbox-direct` (Docker) + `sandbox-e2e` (live web app) |

## Architecture

### Sandbox Client (`sandbox-client.ts`)

Lightweight fetch wrapper purpose-built for the sandbox server's API. Separate from the web app's `api-client.ts` because the sandbox uses its own Bearer token auth (not session cookies/API keys).

Methods: `health()`, `metrics()`, `createSession()`, `getSession()`, `destroySession()`, `executeTool()`, `rawRequest()` (for auth testing without auto-injecting token).

Typed response interfaces: `SandboxHealthResponse`, `SandboxMetricsResponse`, `SandboxSessionResponse`, `SandboxExecuteResponse`.

### Sandbox Context (`sandbox-context.ts`)
