# Separate Sandbox from Custom Executors

## Context

Currently, "sandbox" is one of three executor types (`default | custom_url | sandbox`). This conflates two independent concepts:

- **Executor** = Where tools run (TPMJS default infrastructure, or a user's own server)
- **Sandbox** = A persistent workspace with shell, file, and git tools

A user can't have a custom executor AND a sandbox simultaneously. The goal: any agent can "boot up a sandbox" by flipping a toggle, independent of its executor config.

## Design

- Remove `'sandbox'` from executor types. Executors become: `default | custom_url`
- Add `sandboxEnabled` boolean to the Agent model
- When enabled, 4 sandbox tools (shellExec, readFile, writeFile, listFiles) are **auto-injected** — no manual collection attachment needed
- Sandbox tools always route to the sandbox server; other tools route to the configured executor
- Sandbox URL + API key come from env vars (`AGENT_SANDBOX_URL`, `AGENT_SANDBOX_API_KEY`)

## Files to Modify

### 1. `packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma`

Add to Agent model (after `envVars` line ~647):
```prisma
sandboxEnabled       Boolean    @default(false) @map("sandbox_enabled")
```

### 2. `packages/types/src/executor.ts`

- `ExecutorTypeSchema` → `z.enum(['default', 'custom_url'])` (remove `'sandbox'`)
- Remove `SandboxExecutorConfigSchema` from `ExecutorConfigSchema` discriminated union
- Delete `SandboxExecutorConfig` type export
- Keep all sandbox session types (`CreateSessionRequest/Response`, `DestroySessionResponse`, etc.) — used internally

### 3. `packages/types/src/agent.ts`

- `UpdateAgentSchema`: add `sandboxEnabled: z.boolean().optional()`
- `CreateAgentSchema`: add `sandboxEnabled: z.boolean().default(false).optional()`

### 4. `apps/web/src/lib/executors/index.ts`

- Remove `'sandbox'` case from `parseExecutorConfig()` (lines 106-118)
- Remove sandbox routing from `executeWithExecutor()` (lines 444-456)
- Add new helper:
  ```typescript
  export function getSandboxConfig(): { url: string | null; apiKey: string | undefined } {
    return {
      url: process.env.AGENT_SANDBOX_URL || null,
      apiKey: process.env.AGENT_SANDBOX_API_KEY || undefined,
    };
  }
  ```
- Remove sandbox case from `getExecutorDescription()` (lines 632-644)
- Keep `createSandboxSession()`, `destroySandboxSession()`, `executeWithSandbox()` unchanged

### 5. `apps/web/src/lib/agents/build-tools.ts`

Add `injectSandboxTools(sandboxUrl, sandboxApiKey, sessionId)` function that returns 4 hard-coded tool definitions:

| Tool | Parameters |
|------|-----------|
| `shellExec` | `command` (string, required), `timeout` (number, optional) |
| `readFile` | `path` (string, required) |
| `writeFile` | `path` (string, required), `content` (string, required), `createDirs` (boolean, optional) |
| `listFiles` | `path` (string, optional), `recursive` (boolean, optional), `maxDepth` (number, optional) |

Each tool's `execute()` calls `executeWithSandbox(sandboxUrl, sandboxApiKey, request, sessionId)` directly — bypasses executor resolution.

In `buildAgentTools()`: when `sessionId` is provided, call `injectSandboxTools()` first. Add sandbox tool keys to `seenTools` to deduplicate if the sandbox-shell collection is also attached.

### 6. Conversation Routes (both)

**`apps/web/src/app/api/[username]/agents/[agentSlug]/conversation/[conversationId]/route.ts`**
**`apps/web/src/app/api/agents/[id]/conversation/[conversationId]/route.ts`**

POST handler — replace executor-based sandbox check:
```typescript
// Before: if (agent.executorType === 'sandbox') { parseExecutorConfig... }
// After:
if (agent.sandboxEnabled) {
  const { url: sandboxUrl, apiKey: sandboxApiKey } = getSandboxConfig();
  if (!sandboxUrl) { return 502 error }
  _sandboxUrl = sandboxUrl;
  _sandboxApiKey = sandboxApiKey;
  sessionId = `${agent.id}:${conversationId}`;
  await createSandboxSession(sandboxUrl, sandboxApiKey, sessionId);
}
```

Pass `sandboxUrl` and `sandboxApiKey` to `buildAgentTools()` (new params) so sandbox tools can be injected.

DELETE handler — same pattern:
```typescript
if (agent.sandboxEnabled) {
  const { url: sandboxUrl, apiKey: sandboxApiKey } = getSandboxConfig();
  if (sandboxUrl) {
    destroySandboxSession(sandboxUrl, sandboxApiKey, sessionId).catch(() => {});
  }
}
```

Update `select` clauses: replace `executorType: true, executorConfig: true` with `sandboxEnabled: true` where those were only used for sandbox checks.

### 7. `apps/web/src/components/ExecutorConfigPanel.tsx`

- Remove "Agent Sandbox" radio button (3rd option)
- `ExecutorTypeOption` → `'default' | 'custom_url'`
- Remove `'sandbox'` from `getInitialType`, `getInitialUrl`, `getInitialApiKey`
- Remove sandbox-specific helper text and doc links
- `showUrlFields` → only `executorType === 'custom_url'`

### 8. New: `apps/web/src/components/SandboxToggle.tsx`

Simple toggle with description text:
```
[Switch] Enable Sandbox
Gives your agent a persistent workspace with shell, file, and git tools.
Commands, files, and repos persist across tool calls within each conversation.
```

Props: `enabled: boolean`, `onChange: (enabled: boolean) => void`, `disabled?: boolean`

### 9. `apps/web/src/app/dashboard/agents/[id]/page.tsx`

- Add `<SandboxToggle>` to Settings tab (above executor config panel)
- Status badges: show "Sandbox" badge based on `sandboxEnabled` instead of `executorType === 'sandbox'`
- Wire `sandboxEnabled` into PATCH request on save

### 10. `apps/web/src/app/api/agents/[id]/route.ts`

Handle `sandboxEnabled` in PATCH body → pass to Prisma `update()`.

### 11. `apps/web/src/app/api/agents/[id]/clone/route.ts`

Copy `sandboxEnabled` from source agent (simple boolean, safe to clone).

### 12. Data Migration

```sql
UPDATE agents SET sandbox_enabled = true WHERE executor_type = 'sandbox';
UPDATE agents SET executor_type = NULL, executor_config = NULL WHERE executor_type = 'sandbox';
```

### 13. `apps/web/src/app/docs/executors/sandbox/page.tsx`

Update docs: sandbox is now a toggle, not an executor type. Remove `executorType: 'sandbox'` references.

## Implementation Order

1. Schema: `packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma` + `db:generate` + `db:push`
2. Types: `packages/types/src/executor.ts` + `packages/types/src/agent.ts`
3. Backend: `executors/index.ts` → `build-tools.ts` → both conversation routes → agent PATCH route → clone route
4. Frontend: `ExecutorConfigPanel.tsx` → new `SandboxToggle.tsx` → agent detail page
5. Data migration SQL
6. Type-check + test

## Verification

1. `pnpm --filter=@tpmjs/db db:generate && pnpm --filter=@tpmjs/db db:push`
2. `pnpm type-check`
3. Build + run sandbox Docker container
4. Toggle sandbox on for an agent via the UI
5. Chat with the agent — sandbox tools should appear and work
6. Run sandbox integration tests
7. Verify custom executor still works independently (toggle sandbox + custom URL on same agent)

# Sandbox Integration Tests — CI/CD Plan

## Context

The Agent Sandbox server and shell tools are fully implemented. We need integration tests that:
1. **Layer 1**: Test the sandbox server directly via its HTTP API (Docker container in CI)
2. **Layer 2**: Run the existing E2E test through the TPMJS web app (already written, just needs CI wiring)

## Files to Create

### Helper files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `apps/web/src/test/integration/sandbox/_helpers/sandbox-client.ts` | HTTP client for sandbox server API (health, metrics, sessions, execute-tool, raw requests) |
| `apps/web/src/test/integration/sandbox/_helpers/sandbox-context.ts` | Test context: configures client from env vars, tracks sessions for cleanup, `isSandboxAvailable()` gate |

### Test files (Layer 1 — direct sandbox API)

| File | Tests |
|------|-------|
| `sandbox-health.integration.test.ts` | `GET /health` shape, `GET /metrics` shape, response time |
| `sandbox-sessions.integration.test.ts` | Create, get, resume (idempotent), destroy, 404 on missing, missing sessionId → 400, custom TTL |
| `sandbox-tools.integration.test.ts` | shellExec (echo, exit code, timeout), writeFile+readFile round-trip, createDirs, listFiles root + recursive |
| `sandbox-security.integration.test.ts` | Path traversal `../` blocked for readFile/writeFile, symlink escape blocked, auth 401 when key required, health/metrics allow unauthenticated |
| `sandbox-isolation.integration.test.ts` | Two sessions have separate workspaces, git clone public repo, git init + commit |
| `sandbox-quota.integration.test.ts` | Fill workspace beyond quota → next tool call rejected |

### CI workflow

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `.github/workflows/sandbox-tests.yml` | Two-job workflow: `sandbox-direct` (Docker) + `sandbox-e2e` (live web app) |

## Architecture

### Sandbox Client (`sandbox-client.ts`)

Lightweight fetch wrapper purpose-built for the sandbox server's API. Separate from the web app's `api-client.ts` because the sandbox uses its own Bearer token auth (not session cookies/API keys).

Methods: `health()`, `metrics()`, `createSession()`, `getSession()`, `destroySession()`, `executeTool()`, `rawRequest()` (for auth testing without auto-injecting token).

Typed response interfaces: `SandboxHealthResponse`, `SandboxMetricsResponse`, `SandboxSessionResponse`, `SandboxExecuteResponse`.

### Sandbox Context (`sandbox-context.ts`)

- `isSandboxAvailable()` — checks `SANDBOX_TEST_URL` env var; all Layer 1 tests use `describe.skipIf(!isSandboxAvailable())`
- `getSandboxTestContext()` — returns client, `uniqueSessionId()` generator, session tracker, cleanup function
- Reads `SANDBOX_TEST_URL` and `SANDBOX_TEST_API_KEY` from env

### CI Workflow (`sandbox-tests.yml`)

**Job 1: `sandbox-direct`** (runs on push to main + PRs, path-filtered)
1. Checkout
2. `docker build -t tpmjs-sandbox:test templates/agent-sandbox/`
3. `docker run` with `EXECUTOR_API_KEY=test-ci-key`, `SESSION_DISK_QUOTA_MB=5`, `MAX_CONCURRENT_SESSIONS=10`
4. Wait for `/health` (30 attempts, 2s interval)
5. pnpm install + build
6. Run sandbox-direct test files with `SANDBOX_TEST_URL=http://localhost:3002` and `SANDBOX_TEST_API_KEY=test-ci-key`
7. Show Docker logs on failure
8. Cleanup container

**Job 2: `sandbox-e2e`** (only on push to main, depends on job 1)
1. Checkout + install + build
2. Wait for live web app health
3. Run `sandbox-shell-e2e.integration.test.ts` with all existing secrets + `AGENT_SANDBOX_URL`

Path filters trigger on changes to: `templates/agent-sandbox/**`, `packages/tools/official/sandbox-shell/**`, `apps/web/src/lib/executors/**`, `apps/web/src/test/integration/sandbox/**`.

### setup-integration.ts compatibility

The existing setup file validates `TEST_BASE_URL`, `INTEGRATION_TEST_SESSION_TOKEN`, `INTEGRATION_TEST_API_KEY`. For sandbox-direct tests, we provide dummy values in the CI workflow since those tests never use them.

## Test Details

### Shell exec timeout test
- Command: `sleep 60` with `timeout: 2000`
- Expects exit code 137 (killed) and stderr containing "TIMEOUT"
- Vitest timeout: 15s

### Disk quota test
- CI starts sandbox with `SESSION_DISK_QUOTA_MB=5`
- Test fills workspace with `dd if=/dev/zero of=bigfile.bin bs=1M count=7`
- Next tool call should return `success: false` with error containing "disk quota exceeded"

### Session isolation test
- Creates two sessions, writes file in session 1
- Lists files in session 2 — should NOT contain session 1's file

### Git operations
- Clone `octocat/Hello-World` (small, always available) with `--depth 1`
- Init repo, configure user, create file, commit, verify via `git log`
- 90s vitest timeout for clone

### Security tests
- `readFile` with `../../../etc/passwd` → error "escapes sandbox"
- `writeFile` with `../../tmp/evil.txt` → error "escapes sandbox"
- Create symlink to `/etc/hostname`, readFile via symlink → error "escapes sandbox"
- POST `/sessions` without auth header → 401 (when `EXECUTOR_API_KEY` is set)
- GET `/health` and `/metrics` without auth → 200 (always public)

## Implementation Order

1. `_helpers/sandbox-client.ts`
2. `_helpers/sandbox-context.ts`
3. `sandbox-health.integration.test.ts`
4. `sandbox-sessions.integration.test.ts`
5. `sandbox-tools.integration.test.ts`
6. `sandbox-security.integration.test.ts`
7. `sandbox-isolation.integration.test.ts`
8. `sandbox-quota.integration.test.ts`
9. `.github/workflows/sandbox-tests.yml`

## Verification

1. Build sandbox Docker image: `docker build -t tpmjs-sandbox:test templates/agent-sandbox/`
2. Run sandbox locally: `docker run -d --name sb -p 3002:3002 -e EXECUTOR_API_KEY=dev -e SESSION_DISK_QUOTA_MB=5 tpmjs-sandbox:test`
3. Run tests locally:
   ```bash
   INTEGRATION_TESTS=true \
   SANDBOX_TEST_URL=http://localhost:3002 \
   SANDBOX_TEST_API_KEY=dev \
   SANDBOX_TEST_DISK_QUOTA_MB=5 \
   TEST_BASE_URL=http://localhost:3000 \
   INTEGRATION_TEST_SESSION_TOKEN=dummy \
   INTEGRATION_TEST_API_KEY=dummy \
   pnpm --filter=@tpmjs/web vitest run --config vitest.integration.config.mjs \
     src/test/integration/sandbox/sandbox-health.integration.test.ts \
     src/test/integration/sandbox/sandbox-sessions.integration.test.ts \
     src/test/integration/sandbox/sandbox-tools.integration.test.ts \
     src/test/integration/sandbox/sandbox-security.integration.test.ts \
     src/test/integration/sandbox/sandbox-isolation.integration.test.ts \
     src/test/integration/sandbox/sandbox-quota.integration.test.ts
   ```
4. Type-check: `pnpm --filter=@tpmjs/web type-check`
5. Cleanup: `docker rm -f sb`

## Key Reference Files

- `templates/agent-sandbox/server.ts` — Sandbox server API (all endpoints + response shapes)
- `packages/tools/official/sandbox-shell/src/index.ts` — Tool implementations
- `apps/web/src/test/integration/_helpers/api-client.ts` — Pattern reference
- `apps/web/src/test/integration/_helpers/test-context.ts` — Pattern reference
- `apps/web/src/test/integration/sandbox/sandbox-shell-e2e.integration.test.ts` — Existing E2E test (keep intact)
- `.github/workflows/integration-tests.yml` — CI conventions reference

# Separate Sandbox from Custom Executors

## Context

Currently, "sandbox" is one of three executor types (`default | custom_url | sandbox`). This conflates two independent concepts:

- **Executor** = Where tools run (TPMJS default infrastructure, or a user's own server)
- **Sandbox** = A persistent workspace with shell, file, and git tools

A user can't have a custom executor AND a sandbox simultaneously. The goal: any agent can "boot up a sandbox" by flipping a toggle, independent of its executor config.

## Design

- Remove `'sandbox'` from executor types. Executors become: `default | custom_url`
- Add `sandboxEnabled` boolean to the Agent model
- When enabled, 4 sandbox tools (shellExec, readFile, writeFile, listFiles) are **auto-injected** — no manual collection attachment needed
- Sandbox tools always route to the sandbox server; other tools route to the configured executor
- Sandbox URL + API key come from env vars (`AGENT_SANDBOX_URL`, `AGENT_SANDBOX_API_KEY`)

## Files to Modify

### 1. `packages/db/prisma/schema.prisma`

Add to Agent model (after `envVars` line ~647):
```prisma
sandboxEnabled       Boolean    @default(false) @map("sandbox_enabled")
```

### 2. `packages/types/src/executor.ts`

- `ExecutorTypeSchema` → `z.enum(['default', 'custom_url'])` (remove `'sandbox'`)
- Remove `SandboxExecutorConfigSchema` from `ExecutorConfigSchema` discriminated union
- Delete `SandboxExecutorConfig` type export
- Keep all sandbox session types (`CreateSessionRequest/Response`, `DestroySessionResponse`, etc.) — used internally

### 3. `packages/types/src/agent.ts`

- `UpdateAgentSchema`: add `sandboxEnabled: z.boolean().optional()`
- `CreateAgentSchema`: add `sandboxEnabled: z.boolean().default(false).optional()`

### 4. `apps/web/src/lib/executors/index.ts`

- Remove `'sandbox'` case from `parseExecutorConfig()` (lines 106-118)
- Remove sandbox routing from `executeWithExecutor()` (lines 444-456)
- Add new helper:
  ```typescript
  export function getSandboxConfig(): { url: string | null; apiKey: string | undefined } {
    return {
      url: process.env.AGENT_SANDBOX_URL || null,
      apiKey: process.env.AGENT_SANDBOX_API_KEY || undefined,
    };
  }
  ```
- Remove sandbox case from `getExecutorDescription()` (lines 632-644)
- Keep `createSandboxSession()`, `destroySandboxSession()`, `executeWithSandbox()` unchanged

Add `injectSandboxTools(sandboxUrl, sandboxApiKey, sessionId)` function that returns 4 hard-coded tool definitions:

|------|-----------|
| `shellExec` | `command` (string, required), `timeout` (number, optional) |
| `readFile` | `path` (string, required) |

**`apps/web/src/app/api/agents/[id]/conversation/[conversationId]/route.ts`**

// Before: if (agent.executorType === 'sandbox') { parseExecutorConfig... }
// After:
if (agent.sandboxEnabled) {
  const { url: sandboxUrl, apiKey: sandboxApiKey } = getSandboxConfig();
  if (!sandboxUrl) { return 502 error }
  _sandboxUrl = sandboxUrl;
  _sandboxApiKey = sandboxApiKey;
  sessionId = `${agent.id}:${conversationId}`;
  await createSandboxSession(sandboxUrl, sandboxApiKey, sessionId);
}
```

```typescript
if (agent.sandboxEnabled) {
  const { url: sandboxUrl, apiKey: sandboxApiKey } = getSandboxConfig();
  if (sandboxUrl) {
    destroySandboxSession(sandboxUrl, sandboxApiKey, sessionId).catch(() => {});

}
```

### 7. `apps/web/src/components/ExecutorConfigPanel.tsx`

- Remove "Agent Sandbox" radio button (3rd option)
- `ExecutorTypeOption` → `'default' | 'custom_url'`
- Remove `'sandbox'` from `getInitialType`, `getInitialUrl`, `getInitialApiKey`
